outcome: Capability requests now have one unambiguous current lifecycle
owner_impact: Accepted now means accepted and still waiting in the design queue. As soon as development starts, the current request becomes in progress; once deployed it becomes implemented. Completed requests no longer remain simultaneously accepted. The original Professor acceptance is still preserved in audit history, including reviewer, time and guidance.

next.text: The lifecycle-consistency fix is complete. No owner action is required; future capability-request summaries should classify requests from their current lifecycle state rather than historical Professor decisions.

technical_evidence: Database constraints forbid accepted disposition on in-progress or implemented requests.
Development claim/completion functions clear the live accepted disposition automatically while append-only Professor review history remains unchanged.
Existing implemented requests are reconciled to implemented-only current state.
Professor inbox renders the canonical current lifecycle, and MCP capability-request interface v9 declares request_status as the current-state authority.
Every MCP capability-request contract reference is aligned on vlab.capability-request/9.
Historical regression tests were advanced from the superseded v8/3.15 and disposition-as-current-state contract to the v9/3.16 single-current-lifecycle contract.
Migration ordering is guarded: the legacy consistency rule is dropped before advanced rows are normalized, and the stricter rule is installed only afterward.
